landmarks.name: Al Baleed
landmarks.text: Al Baleed is an archaeological park on the coast of Salalah. It is the ruins of the ancient city of Zafar, a busy port from about the 10th to the 15th century. Ships from India and China came here for frankincense, and the port also exported Arabian horses. Today visitors ride around the ruins in electric carts or small boats on the lagoon. The Museum of the Frankincense Land stands next to the park. Al Baleed is one of the four sites of the Land of Frankincense, which became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

landmarks.name: Mughsail Beach
landmarks.text: Mughsail is a long white beach about 40 kilometres west of Salalah. At the eastern end of the beach, under the rocks of Marneef Cave, there are natural holes in the stone called blowholes. When a wave hits the rocks below, sea water is pushed up through the holes and shoots many metres into the air with a loud noise. The blowholes are strongest during the khareef, when the sea is rough. Families come to Mughsail for picnics, and the road west of the beach climbs the cliffs in sharp bends towards the Yemen border.

landmarks.name: Ayn Razat
landmarks.text: Ayn Razat is a natural spring about 25 kilometres north-east of Salalah, at the foot of the mountains. Water flows from the rock all year and feeds a small garden with trees, grass and a stream. It is one of the most popular picnic places in Dhofar, especially on Friday afternoons. Above the spring there is a small cave that visitors can climb to. During the khareef the hills around Ayn Razat are covered in cloud, and the stream becomes much stronger.

landmarks.name: Wadi Dawkah
landmarks.text: Wadi Dawkah is a dry valley about 40 kilometres north of Salalah, on the other side of the mountains. It is a natural park of frankincense trees, Boswellia sacra, with more than a thousand old trees and many young ones planted in recent years. The trees grow here because the khareef rain does not reach this side of the mountains and the ground is dry and stony. In spring, collectors make small cuts in the bark, and the white sap hardens into frankincense. The valley is one of the four sites of the Land of Frankincense.

landmarks.name: Taqah Castle
landmarks.text: Taqah is a fishing town about 35 kilometres east of Salalah. Its castle was built in the 19th century as the home of the wali, the local governor, and his family. Today the castle is a museum. Visitors can see the governor's rooms, the kitchen, the prison and the tower, with old guns, coffee pots and photographs. The town is famous for sardines, which are dried in the sun on the beach and sold as food for camels and cows. In the khareef, the hills behind Taqah are the first to turn green.

landmarks.name: Sumhuram (Khor Rori)
landmarks.text: Sumhuram is an ancient city on a hill above the lagoon of Khor Rori, east of Taqah. It was founded more than 2,000 years ago as a port for the frankincense trade. Ships sailed from here to India, and traders from Egypt and Rome bought the resin in the city's market. The stone walls, the gate and the temple can still be seen today. Over the centuries a bank of sand closed the lagoon, so ships could no longer enter, and the city was abandoned. Today flamingos and other birds live on the water, and the site is part of the Land of Frankincense.

landmarks.name: Wadi Darbat
landmarks.text: Wadi Darbat is a green valley in the mountains north of Taqah. In the khareef, water from the hills collects in a lake and then falls over a cliff about 100 metres high, making the most famous waterfall in Oman. Visitors rent small boats on the lake, and camels and cows walk freely between the picnic tables. The valley is cool and misty from July to September, so thousands of families from the Gulf drive here every weekend. In winter the waterfall is dry, but the lake and the trees remain.

landmarks.name: Tawi Atair Sinkhole
landmarks.text: Tawi Atair means 'the well of birds'. It is a giant sinkhole in the mountains between Wadi Darbat and Jabal Samhan, about 200 metres deep and more than 100 metres wide. It was formed over thousands of years when rain water slowly dissolved the limestone rock until the roof of a cave fell in. Hundreds of birds nest on the walls, and their songs echo from the bottom, which gives the place its name. A path and a viewing platform let visitors look down into the hole safely, but climbing down is dangerous and not allowed.

landmarks.name: Mirbat Castle
landmarks.text: Mirbat is an old port town about 70 kilometres east of Salalah. For centuries its ships carried frankincense and Arabian horses to India and East Africa, and the name Mirbat comes from an Arabic word for the place where horses are tied. The small castle near the harbour was built in the 19th century to protect the port, and it is now a museum. In the old town, merchant houses with carved wooden doors show how rich the traders once were. Nearby stands the white tomb of Bin Ali, a famous teacher who lived in the 14th century.

landmarks.name: Jabal Samhan
landmarks.text: Jabal Samhan is the highest mountain in Dhofar, about 2,100 metres above the sea. From the viewpoint at the top, visitors can see the whole coast from Mirbat to Sadah and, on clear days, ships far out in the Indian Ocean. The mountain became a nature reserve in 1997 to protect the Arabian leopard, one of the rarest animals in the world, as well as wolves, foxes and hundreds of plants. The road to the top is steep, with many sharp bends, and in the khareef it is often hidden in thick fog, so drivers must go slowly.

qs.why: 'became a nature reserve in 1997'
qs.evidence: became a nature reserve in 1997

scene: Above the clouds, where the leopard walks, the last stone stands upright on the edge of the cliff.
SAMHAN. The five names are together again.
The Road of Frankincense is complete. Chapter 1 is finished.

offline_checkpoints.text: The khareef festival in Salalah runs from the middle of July to the end of August. There are concerts, markets and a traditional village. Entrance to the festival park costs one rial for adults and is free for children under six.
offline_checkpoints.q: How much is the entrance for adults? (a number)

offline_checkpoints.text: Omani halwa is a sweet made from sugar, starch, water, rose water and nuts. In Salalah the best shops are near the Al Husn souq. The halwa is cooked for about two hours in a large copper pot.
offline_checkpoints.q: How long is the halwa cooked? (a number)

offline_checkpoints.text: Fog lights help drivers in the khareef, but many visitors forget to turn them on. Fog is thickest on the mountain roads in the early morning and in the evening. The road to Jabal Samhan can be closed when the fog is very thick.

offline_checkpoints.why: 'thickest ... in the early morning and in the evening'

offline_checkpoints.text: Dried sardines from Taqah are sold in large bags along the road. Farmers mix them with dates and water to feed their camels in the dry months. One bag weighs about 20 kilograms.
offline_checkpoints.q: How much does one bag weigh? (a number)

offline_checkpoints.text: Salalah airport opened its new terminal in 2015. In the khareef season, extra flights arrive every day from Muscat, Dubai and Doha. Most visitors rent a car at the airport, so the roads are busy at the weekend.

offline_checkpoints.text: The coconut farms of Salalah are the only ones in Arabia. Coconut water is sold cold on the roadside for half a rial. The trees grow here because the ground water is close to the surface and the khareef keeps the air damp.
offline_checkpoints.q: Coconut trees grow in Salalah because
opts: the ground water is close to the surface.
offline_checkpoints.why: 'because the ground water is close to the surface'

offline_checkpoints.text: The Marneef Cave viewpoint at Mughsail has a small cafe. It opens at 8 in the morning and closes at sunset. Visitors are asked not to stand near the blowholes, because the water can knock a person over.
offline_checkpoints.q: What time does the cafe open? (a number)

offline_checkpoints.text: Frankincense is burned in Omani homes to welcome guests. The resin is placed on hot charcoal in a clay burner called a majmar. A kilogram of the best hojari grade can cost more than 30 rials.
offline_checkpoints.q: What is the clay burner called?

offline_checkpoints.text: The road from Salalah to Thumrait crosses the mountains and then the desert. There are no petrol stations for about 80 kilometres, so drivers fill the tank before they leave. The temperature in the desert can be 20 degrees higher than in Salalah.
offline_checkpoints.q: Drivers fill the tank before they leave because
opts: there are no petrol stations for a long way.
offline_checkpoints.why: 'no petrol stations for about 80 kilometres, so drivers fill the tank'

offline_checkpoints.text: Wadi Darbat has a large car park, but at the weekend it is full by 10 o'clock. Buses from the car park take visitors to the waterfall every 15 minutes. The ticket costs 500 baisa.
offline_checkpoints.q: How often do the buses run? Every ... minutes (a number)

offline_checkpoints.text: Fishermen in Mirbat leave the harbour at 4 in the morning and return at midday. They catch tuna, kingfish and lobster. The fish is sold at the Salalah fish market, 70 kilometres away, the same afternoon.

The Sultan Qaboos Mosque in Salalah is the largest mosque in Dhofar. It was opened in 2009 and can hold thousands of people. Visitors are welcome in the morning, but they must dress modestly and remove their shoes.
offline_checkpoints.q: When was the mosque opened? (a year)

offline_checkpoints.text: The Land of Frankincense Museum at Al Baleed has two halls. The History Hall shows the story of Oman, and the Maritime Hall shows models of dhows and the sea routes to India and Africa. The museum is closed on Fridays.
offline_checkpoints.why: 'models of dhows and the sea routes'

offline_checkpoints.text: Baobab trees grow in Wadi Hinna, east of Mirbat. These huge trees come from Africa and are more than 500 years old. The fruit is dried and used as a sour powder in drinks.
offline_checkpoints.q: How old are the trees? More than ... years (a number)

offline_checkpoints.text: Driving at night in the mountains is dangerous because cows sleep on the warm road. Local drivers use the horn before every bend. Visitors are advised to return to the city before dark.
offline_checkpoints.q: Night driving in the mountains is dangerous because
offline_checkpoints.why: 'because cows sleep on the warm road'
